usage.callShape: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/minerva/resolve with JSON body {records:[{record_id, first_name, last_name, email?, phone?}]}
usage.outputShape: body.results[] (each: {record_id, is_match, minerva_pid, linkedin_url, match_score, is_resolvable_record, validation_errors}); body.api_request_id; body.request_completed_at
quirks: Input is wrapped in a records[] array, NOT a flat object; output comes back in results[] keyed by the same record_id you sent.

Name-only records return is_match:false / is_resolvable_record:false with validation_errors.contact='No valid emails or phones were provided' — supply an email and/or phone in each record to actually resolve a person.
Always returns HTTP 200 even on a non-match; check results[].is_match (not status code) to know if it found someone.
Pay-per-call x402 on Base, $0.02/call charged regardless of match outcome.
usage.guide: POST to https://stableenrich.dev/api/minerva/resolve with body {records:[{record_id, first_name, last_name, email, phone}]} — pay x402 ($0.02/call on Base, no API key). For a real match include an email and/or phone; name-only records will not resolve. Read results from body.results[], matching on record_id; check is_match before using minerva_pid/linkedin_url. Sibling endpoints: /enrich (records[] by pid/linkedin_url/name → demographics/contact/financial, $0.05, use return_fields to trim) and /validate-emails (array of email strings, $0.01). Response is synchronous JSON; always HTTP 200 so gate on results[].is_match, not the status code.
